caption:
Referrals aren't luck.

They're a systems failure most owners never notice.

A widely cited referral marketing study found 83% of happy customers say they'd refer a business, but only 29% ever do.

That gap isn't a customer problem. It's timing and friction.

1. You ask after the invoice, when the moment has passed

2. When you do ask, it's a vague "tell your friends" with no easy way to act on it

Fix both this week.

Ask at the reveal, the moment they see the finished work, not after they've paid and moved on.

Then hand them one link they can text in ten seconds. No login, no memory required.

Build the ask into the process. Referrals stop being random.

The Black Arrow platform tracks every referral, so you know who sent who.

rationale: Reframes referrals from luck to a fixable process gap, using a properly qualified third-party stat and a concrete two-step fix that a service owner can implement this week.
